spans.text: ■FILE■ PACC78493721872567, decrypting...
Beep.
A surveillance footage from Beslan Primary School No.6 starts playing.
...Sana, it's already 1835. I told your mother to come to the meeting at 1800, didn't I?
Sorry... Mama is very busy with work...
Doesn't your mother work as a teacher at High School No.1? I have friends there, and they've all got off work by now.
Sana sits obediently on the chair, staring at her toes without saying a word. The teacher sighs and puts down the communicator that no one has picked up despite countless calls.
Other than seeing your mother briefly at the start of the semester, we haven't seen her since.
I do understand how hard it is to be a single parent and a teacher... That said, school arrangements still need to be respected.
I've heard that instead of paying attention to top-performing students, your mother seems more invested in the ones at the bottom of the class.
If only she'd spare even half that attention for you.
The teacher opens the thin notebook in front of her.
Since your parent isn't here, I'll have to speak with you directly. I'll write a note for your mother later.
Make sure to tell her that the school board is very displeased with her repeated absences from parent meetings.
Okay...
Sana, you've picked up Russian very quickly. You don't seem to have any trouble with classes or daily conversation now.
Your Russian compositions this term were excellent—the Russian teacher specifically asked me to commend you.
...Thank you.
All of your grades this term are A's—very impressive.
Especially your math—you scored full marks.
However, you scored zero for physical education. The PE teacher says you've missed every group training session.
You're too withdrawn. Several classmates have told me that you're very aloof, always keeping to yourself, and that you're never around during group activities.
You can't live in your own little world forever. Next semester, try to be more outgoing and make some friends.
But...
Sana, who has kept her head down the whole time, lifts it in frustration and looks at the teacher across from her.
They don't like me...
Whenever I go near them, they call me a filthy American spy...
Sometimes when I walk past them, they shove me away really hard...
The teacher raises her eyebrows slightly, then quickly flips a page to cover Sana's barely audible voice.
There's no more to discuss. That'll be all for today.
Okay. Thank you, teacher!
Like a wind-up toy, Sana—who looked like she was about to cry just moments ago—suddenly springs out of her seat, slings her backpack on, and rushes for the door.
Your mother hasn't come to pick you up yet. Where are you going?
I'm going to Anna's house!
